question: Indicate which characteristic of the whiplash direction of the nystagmus is characteristic of an acute peripheral non-positional vestibular syndrome:

options.opa: With visual fixation and in the primary position of the gaze changes or alternates the direction spontaneously and periodically.
options.opb: With visual fixation, it changes direction when looking to one side or the other.
options.opc: With visual fixation and in the primary position of the gaze it is vertical downwards pure, without horizontal component.
options.opd: Both with visual fixation and when canceling it is unidirectional.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Acute peripheral vestibular syndrome" -> "nystagmus present" -> "nystagmus is typically unidirectional" -> "both with visual fixation and when canceling it is unidirectional" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Acute peripheral vestibular syndrome" -> "nystagmus observed" -> "nystagmus direction is consistent" -> "does not change with visual fixation" -> "unidirectional" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Acute peripheral vestibular syndrome" -> "nystagmus characteristics analyzed" -> "nystagmus is unidirectional" -> "remains unidirectional with visual fixation" -> "supports option (opd)" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Acute peripheral vestibular syndrome" -> "nystagmus direction assessed" -> "nystagmus is not vertical or alternating" -> "indicates unidirectional nature" -> "confirms option (opd)" -> 85%
analysis: In acute peripheral vestibular syndromes, nystagmus is typically unidirectional and does not change direction with visual fixation. This aligns with option opd, which states that the nystagmus is unidirectional both with and without visual fixation. Other options describe characteristics that are not typical of acute peripheral vestibular syndromes.
